issues.issue: Unsynced events can be stranded forever when the device id and the event log live in different durability domains. `dev` is in localStorage (warriorlog.settings) while events are in IndexedDB, and PUSH step 1 selects `synced=0 AND dev === settings.dev`. If localStorage is lost/regenerated while IDB survives (Safari 'Clear website data' partial clears, a 'Forget token'/reset flow that rewrites settings, or Export→Import onto a new phone whose settings.dev differs from the exported events' dev), every unsynced event carrying the old dev is excluded from the push forever, the nav dot shows nothing wrong (the amber count may or may not include them), and the events are lost on the next storage eviction. Import to a replacement phone is exactly the recovery path the design advertises, and it silently drops anything that had not been pushed by the old phone.
issues.evidence: storage_and_sync.local: 'localStorage warriorlog.settings holds only dev, user, token…'; sync_algorithm PUSH step 1: 'Select events where synced=0 AND dev === settings.dev'; data_model: 'dev: 6-char device id generated once per browser install'; settings view 'Export/Import JSON' as the disaster-recovery path. No step migrates or re-partitions foreign-dev unsynced events.
issues.fix: (a) Persist `dev` in the IDB meta store (same durability domain as events) and treat localStorage as a cache of it. (b) Change PUSH step 1 to select `synced=0 AND (private=false OR syncMetrics)` regardless of dev, grouping by the event's own (user,dev,month) partition, and PUT to log/<event.user>/<event.dev>/<month>.jsonl. This is safe: the path's 'sole writer' may be gone, and if it is not, the sha check forces the 409 → GET → union-by-id → PUT path, which is a monotone union and cannot lose either side. (c) On Import, mark imported events synced=0 only when their id is not already known remotely (run a Pull-all first), then flush. (d) Add a sync.test.js case: 'unsynced events with a dev that is not settings.dev are still pushed to their own partition'.

issues.issue: PULL permanently drops partner events it cannot validate, and the sha bookkeeping makes the gap sticky. PULL step 3 'migrateEvent each, validate, insert events whose id is unknown' then 'record files[path] = {sha,…}'. When Cat's phone is on a newer shell (new event type, or `v` > this phone's SCHEMA_VERSION — migrateEvent only upgrades, it cannot downgrade) and Sean's is one launch stale — the exact window the SW design accepts on every deploy — Sean's phone rejects those lines, still records the file's sha as fetched, and never re-reads the file unless its sha changes. A month file whose month has ended never changes sha again, so those events are missing from Sean's scoreboard, duo streak and boss progress permanently (until a manual Pull-all, if that ignores shas — unspecified). The same applies to tolerant-parse skips ('skip and count bad lines').
issues.evidence: sync_algorithm PULL step 2: 'For each path whose tree sha differs from files[path].sha'; step 3: 'Parse JSONL tolerantly (skip and count bad lines), migrateEvent each, validate, insert events whose id is unknown … record files[path] = {sha, fetchedAt}'; events.js: 'MIGRATIONS[] + migrateEvent()' (upgrade only); pwa_and_mobile: 'at most one stale launch per deploy'.
issues.fix: Never drop on pull: store every parsed line as-is (keep its `v` and raw type) and have reduce() skip events it does not understand, so the next shell update re-derives with them included. If any line still fails to parse, do not advance files[path].sha (or store {sha, partial:true}) so the file is refetched next pull. Make Settings → Pull all ignore files[*].sha explicitly. Add a sync test: 'event with v=SCHEMA_VERSION+1 from a partner file is persisted and reduce ignores it; after bumping SCHEMA_VERSION it is applied without a refetch'.

issues.issue: The app's one-tap 'Create data branch' fallback does not create an orphan branch — it creates `data` from main's head, so the data branch would carry the entire app (index.html, sw.js, src/, .nojekyll) and every subsequent log commit descends from app code. This contradicts the orphan invariant in CLAUDE.md, makes the branch diverge from the laptop-created orphan if deploy step 7 is run later (push rejected / confusion about which is canonical), and means a later laptop `git push -f origin data` of the real orphan branch would orphan the phones' commits.
issues.evidence: storage_and_sync.remote: 'app can self-create it via POST /repos/{o}/{r}/git/refs {ref:"refs/heads/data", sha:<main head>}'; PUSH step 7: 'GET …/git/ref/heads/main → POST …/git/refs {"ref":"refs/heads/data","sha":"<main sha>"}'; deploy step 7 creates a true orphan with `git checkout --orphan data && git rm -rf .`.
issues.fix: Either remove the in-app fallback (deploy step 7 is mandatory and the 404 diagnosis just says 'data branch missing — run deploy step 7') or build a real orphan via the Git Database API, which the same Contents:write permission covers: POST /git/blobs (README) → POST /git/trees → POST /git/commits with parents:[] → POST /git/refs refs/heads/data. Pin with a sync test that the created commit has zero parents.

issues.issue: An expired/revoked token (a guaranteed annual event with 366-day expiry) also stops PULL, so the partner status, scoreboard, duo streak and boss progress freeze on that phone even though the repo is public and needs no auth to read. Risk #3 only says 'workouts keep logging locally'; the duo features silently go stale.
issues.evidence: PUSH step 8: '401 or 403 … settings.tokenState="invalid", stop the queue'; all requests use 'Authorization: Bearer <settings.token>' including PULL; GitHub returns 401 for any request bearing an invalid token even on public repos.
issues.fix: On tokenState='invalid' (and when no token is set), keep pulling without an Authorization header — the tree GET with If-None-Match and 1–3 raw content GETs per open fit easily in the 60 req/h unauthenticated budget. Only push is blocked. Note the docs now allow expires_in='none'; keeping 366 days is a defensible security choice but should be stated as one.

issues.issue: Public-repo leakage slightly exceeds what the design claims. profile.updated carries `tz` ('America/Chicago') and session.finished carries free-text `note`; both are pushed to a public branch, while risks #4 says 'no locations or emails beyond the display addresses'. Timezone plus the `day`/`ts` pattern of every session publicly reveals where and when the couple is at home. Also, once syncMetrics is turned on, metrics-<month>.jsonl is in public git history permanently even after turning it off.
issues.evidence: data_model: profile.updated {"tz":"America/Chicago"…}; session.finished {"note":"swings felt good"}; risks #4 'no locations'; remote: 'Optional log/<user>/<dev>/metrics-<yyyy-mm>.jsonl only when syncMetrics is on'.
issues.fix: Strip `tz` at the sync boundary (it is only used locally; the design already assumes both users share a timezone for the shared week). Show a one-line 'notes are public on GitHub' hint on the Finish sheet and in Body → syncMetrics opt-in add 'this cannot be un-published (git history)'. Add a sync test asserting `tz` never appears in serialized content.

issues.issue: The token test can pass with a token that cannot write. GET /repos/{o}/{r} returns `permissions.push` for the authenticated user (SJJ363 is org owner → always true), not for the fine-grained token's granted permissions, so a Contents:read-only or wrong-repo-scoped token shows 'Connected … write' and only fails at the first real PUT after a workout.
issues.evidence: TOKEN TEST: 'GET /repos/{O}/{R} → 200 and permissions.push===true … show "Connected as <login> · write · data branch OK"'.
issues.fix: Treat the Settings test as connectivity only and make the first push the write test with an explicit 403 banner ('token has no Contents:write'), or perform the real flush immediately after Save when unsynced>0. Alternatively check the response's x-accepted-github-permissions header is absent on a probing PUT; do not rely on `permissions.push`.

issues.issue: Pull-triggered full re-render during an active session can interrupt one-tap logging. PULL fires on visibilitychange→visible and after every push (push fires on visibilitychange→hidden), so returning to the app mid-workout after a notification runs pull → reduce → render() → root.innerHTML replaced, discarding an open bottom sheet's uncontrolled stepper values and restarting keyed DOM for the rest-timer ring.
issues.evidence: TRIGGERS: 'pull … on visibilitychange→visible … and after every successful push'; PULL step 4: 'Recompute … render'; rendering_and_state: 'root.innerHTML replaced', 'text inputs are uncontrolled and read on submit'.
issues.fix: While settings.activeSessionId is set, let pull write to IDB and recompute partner/duo state but skip render() unless the current route is not the session (or only patch the partner chip). Render the merged state on Finish/route change.

issues.issue: The 'Cat's sets can never fold into Sean's ladders' guarantee relies solely on the `user` field inside each pulled line; PULL does not check that event.user/event.dev match the path's <user>/<dev>. A Switch-user closure bug on one phone (writing user:'sean' events into log/cat/<dev>/) or a hand-edited file would be reduced into the wrong user's state on both phones.
issues.evidence: PULL step 3 validates the event shape only; remote layout 'log/<user>/<dev>/<yyyy-mm>.jsonl'; overview 'reduce() partitions by user'. No path↔envelope consistency check is specified.
issues.fix: In PULL step 3 drop (and count/report) any line whose event.user or event.dev differs from the path segments and whose month (from `day`) differs from the file's month; add the same assertion to the push serializer and a test.

issues.issue: The partition month key is unspecified: `part = user/dev/month` and the file is <yyyy-mm>.jsonl, but events carry both `ts` (UTC) and `day` (local). Deriving month from ts on one code path and from day on another puts near-midnight events in a file whose name differs from their index, breaking the 'content = ALL local events for that partition' rewrite (an event could be written to two files, or to none).
issues.evidence: data_model: 'part = user+"/"+dev+"/"+month'; 'day: LOCAL calendar day… ts: UTC instant'; PUSH step 2 'ALL local events for that partition'.
issues.fix: Define month = day.slice(0,7) once in util.monthKey(event) and use it for the IDB index, the push grouping and the pull consistency check; pin with a util test at a DST/midnight boundary.

summary: The GitHub-facing claims hold up against the docs: Contents PUT returns 409 on a stale sha and needs `sha` to update, `author` is honoured with committer defaulting to the token owner, `ref` accepts a branch name and the raw media type reads up to 100 MB; fine-grained PATs can target an org-owned repo when the user is a member, org-owner-created tokens are auto-approved, and 366 days is the max custom expiry (with `none` now also allowed); branch-source Pages only publish on pushes to the publishing branch, so orphan `data` commits never rebuild the site. The architecture's sole-writer partitions plus union-by-id merge are sound for two phones. It is refuted on two data-integrity paths in its own bookkeeping: (1) push filters unsynced events by `settings.dev` (localStorage) while events live in IDB, so a lost/regenerated dev id or an Export→Import to a new phone strands unsynced events forever; (2) pull validates-and-drops partner events it cannot parse/migrate (newer schema from the partner's already-updated shell, i.e. every deploy window) yet still records the file sha, so closed month files leave permanent holes in the partner's history. Both have contained fixes (dev in IDB meta + push by event partition; store unknown events raw and never advance sha on partial reads). Lesser issues: the in-app 'Create data branch' fallback makes a non-orphan branch, an expired token needlessly blocks public-repo pulls, `tz` and free-text notes are published contrary to the stated privacy claim, the token test cannot detect a read-only token, pull-triggered re-render can interrupt an in-progress set entry, and path↔event consistency and the month key are unspecified.
